findings.title: Thundering herd: no re-check of cache after acquiring write lock
findings.body: After acquiring the write lock at line 48, the function does not re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache has been populated by another goroutine that passed the fast-path check (lines 41-47) while the cache was still nil. As a result, every concurrent goroutine that observes a nil cache in the fast path will acquire the write lock in turn and each redundantly re-read the manifest file and re-parse the JSON. This is the classic double-checked-locking pitfall: the fast-path RLock/RUnlock check at lines 41-43 is not mirrored inside the Lock-held critical section. At Grafana startup, where many HTTP handlers can call this function concurrently, this causes N redundant file reads and JSON decodes instead of one. The fix is to add a re-check inside the write-lock critical section, e.g. by inserting `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` on line 48.

findings.title: No regression test added for the race fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the entryPointAssetsCache package variable by adding a sync.RWMutex around its reads and writes. However, no test file is added or modified alongside this change. A regression test that calls GetWebAssets concurrently from multiple goroutines (e.g. via sync.WaitGroup) and runs under `go test -race` would have caught the original race and now guards against future refactors reintroducing it. Without such a test, the fix is unverified by CI and can silently regress.
